title: The 12-lead ECG
summary: A standard 12-lead ECG of a healthy 29-year-old man.
description: Thirty seconds of a resting 12-lead ECG. The six limb leads (I, II, III, aVR, aVL and aVF) look at the heart's electrical activity in the frontal plane, and the six chest leads (V1 to V6) in the horizontal plane. The same beats look different in each lead, because each lead records the heart's electrical activity from a different direction.
look_for: The QRS points up in lead II and down in aVR
How the R wave grows from V1 to V6 (the R-wave progression)
Einthoven's law: at any moment, the voltage of lead II is the sum of those of leads I and III

beats.note: The beats were found automatically by the workbench (the R waves of Lead II), and checked by eye, but not by a cardiologist.

subject.notes: A healthy volunteer (a control of the PTB database).
